label: copy-phase input f (mid-sequence)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost only when the fed-back input is f (98% of activation mass; a little on j, usually right after f). It never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on the first occurrence of a token. Plain copy-phase f has recall 0.96 and mass recall 0.98, but only 17% of copy-phase f steps activate (F1 0.29). Firing is strongest mid-copy: recall_idx 3-5 with at least 3 outputs still to go, which is where the F1 0.53 predicate comes from, and it is stronger for longer sequences (L 8-9). Magnitude is highest when the next token being output is j: f followed by j gives the top examples, and that subset has precision 0.72. Other next outputs (c, e, z, b, t, 3) also raise the rate. Copy-phase f near the start or end of the copy, or in short sequences, is mostly inactive. The rest of the variance in precision was not captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, j, z, b, c, -; least: v, w, a, m) and the token being output (most: j, f, e, c, z, b; least: m, l, x, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=9 & t=13.
